extracted.intended_audience: general public — lay caregivers, nurses, parents, first-aid providers
extracted.subtask_short: first aid and contagious disease care
extracted.subtask_description: Practical first-aid and home-care guidance for burns, frostbite, fainting, suffocation, convulsions, ingrowing toenails, chilblains, and eruptive contagious fevers (scarlet fever, measles, German measles). Includes immediate emergency steps, subsequent wound care, and isolation/reporting guidance for infectious diseases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous warm-water immersion for burns
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep temperature even by allowing warm water to continually run into the tub to displace that which runs out (can be arranged by siphonage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This method requires more care and running hot and cold water, but is the most comfortable treatment for severe burns, usually attended by awful suffering, and at the same time it is most favorable to healing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burn by strong acid — neutralize then control pain
rubrics_metrics.description: First Aid Rule 1.--Neutralize the acid. Scatter baking soda thickly over burn, or pour limewater over it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 2.--Control pain. Wash off soda with stream of water. Apply Carron oil (equal parts of limewater and linseed oil or olive oil). Bandage lightly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burn by strong alkali — neutralize then control pain
rubrics_metrics.description: First Aid Rule 1.--Neutralize the alkali. Pour vinegar over the burn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 2.--Control pain. Wash off vinegar with stream of water. Dry gently. Apply vaseline or cold cream.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment for burns caused by strong mineral acids or alkalies (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: If acids are the cause, the skin should not be washed at first, but either chalk, whiting, or some mild alkali, as baking soda, should be strewn over the burn; then after neutralization wash off the soda with stream of warm water.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dry gently with gauze. Apply Carron oil or paste of boric acid and vaseline, equal parts. If strong alkalies have been spilled on the skin (ammonia, potash, quicklime), then vinegar is proper, followed by washing. Dry gently. Vaseline or cold cream is usually sufficient as after treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eye contamination with acids or alkalies
rubrics_metrics.description: Limewater is useful in counteracting the effect of acids spattered in the eye. In the case of alkalies in the eye, the vinegar used should be diluted with three parts of water.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Albolene or liquid vaseline is the best agent to drop in the eye after either accident, to relieve irritation and pain, and the patient should stay in a dark room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frostbite (real freezing) — restore circulation by rubbing
rubrics_metrics.description: First Aid Rule 1.--Restore circulation. Rub gently, then vigorously, with snow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The goal is to re-establish blood flow to frozen tissues while avoiding excessive injury from rubbing; begin gently and increase as circulation returns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frostbite — gradual rewarming (avoid sudden heat)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 2.--Restore heat very gradually. Sudden heat is fatal. Keep in cold room, and rub with cloth wet with very cold water till circulation is established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Then rub with equal parts of alcohol and water and expose gradually to heat of living room. Avoid sudden warming which increases inflammatory sequel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artificial respiration (manual resuscitation technique)
rubrics_metrics.description: If person ceases to breathe, resuscitate as if drowned: open mouth, grasp tongue, pull it forward and keep it there; assistant draws arms up beside head; third assistant astride hips performs timed compressions and releases to imitate natural breathing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed procedure: assistant at hips grasps body, places thumbs by pit of stomach, uses knees as pivot and leans forward to compress slowly for about five seconds, then suddenly lets go; the head assistant draws arms up and holds for about five seconds; repeat deliberately 12–15 times per minute. Continue artificial respiration from one to four hours or until patient breathes; persist and warm body after return of breathing with warm-water bottles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frostbite — subsequent care and necrotic tissue management
rubrics_metrics.description: After circulation resumes, rub with alcohol-and-water, give warm drinks, raise frozen hand/foot on pillows and cover with absorbent cotton and bandage; if redness, swelling, and pain result remove dressing and wrap in a single thickness of cotton kept wet with alcohol-and-water.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsequent care: keep parts covered with vaseline or cold cream, absorbent cotton, and bandage. If blisters/sores occur, treat as for burns. If death of the frozen part is inevitable, suspend the hand or foot nearly vertically to keep blood out, bathe twice daily with corrosive sublimate solution (one 7.7 gr. tablet to pint of water), dust with aristol, and dress until dead tissue separates; large dead parts may be removed surgically but not required for tips of fingers/toes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resuscitation after apparent death from freezing
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons found apparently frozen to death should be brought into a cold room, which should be gradually heated, and the body rubbed with snow or ice water, and artificial respiration employed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attempts at resuscitation ought to be persistent; recoveries have been reported after several hours of unconsciousness and apparent death from freezing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chilblains — prevention (clothing and habits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Susceptible persons should wear thick, warm (not rough) stockings and warm gloves. The chilled members must never be suddenly warmed. Regular exercise and cold shower baths are good to strengthen the circulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid washing hands/feet in very hot water; wash in warm water only and dry thoroughly. Exposure to cold will immediately bring on recurrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chilblains — topical and internal treatments
rubrics_metrics.description: If sweating of these parts is common, dust starch or zinc oxide night and morning. Cod-liver oil is an efficacious remedy — one teaspoonful of Peter Moeller's pure oil three times daily after meals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affected parts are bathed twice daily in a solution of zinc acetate (one dram to one pint of water), followed by application on soft linen or cotton of zinc-oxide ointment containing two percent carbolic acid. If not curative, try iodine ointment mixed with equal quantity of lard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chilblains with blisters or sores — treat like burns
rubrics_metrics.description: If the parts become blistered and open sores appear, then the same treatment as for burns is indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wash with a weak solution of corrosive sublimate (one tablet for surgical purposes in two quarts of warm water) and apply an ointment of boric acid and vaseline, equal parts, on soft, clean cotton or linen; rest of the part and warm atmosphere will complete cure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ingrowing toenail — prevention and nail care
rubrics_metrics.description: Improper footgear is the most common cause; nails should be cut straight across, and not trimmed away at the corners to follow the outline of the toes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Properly fitting footwear (broad at toes, low heels, sufficient length) prevents recurrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ingrowing toenail — conservative home treatment and indications for surgery
rubrics_metrics.description: If pus forms, raise the cut edge by pushing absorbent cotton under the nail daily. Use hot poultices, frequent hot-water soaks, and maintain cleanliness. Dust tannic acid or antiseptic powder like nosophen along the nail edge; push in cotton with tannic acid to crowd flesh away.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If raw surface appears, dust powdered lead nitrate each morning for 4–5 days until ulcerated tissue shrinks. Cover with absorbent cotton and bandage. As soon as the toe is really inflamed the case becomes surgical and demands the care of a surgeon when obtainable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fainting — immediate first aid
rubrics_metrics.description: First Aid Rule 1.--Remove impediments to respiration: remove collar, loosen all waist bands and cords, unhook corset or cut laces at person's back.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 2.--Assist heart and brain with blood pressure: put cushion under buttocks, wind skirt close about legs, and raise feet in air; wait ten seconds. Rule 3.--Aid respiration: put mild smelling salts under nose, spatter cold water in face.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suffocation from gas — immediate steps
rubrics_metrics.description: First Aid Rule 1.--Remove quickly into pure air.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 2.--Resuscitate as if drowned (see detailed artificial respiration). Rule 3.--Give oxygen to breathe from a cylinder, for two days, at short intervals, in the case of illuminating gas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fit/Convulsion — first-aid steps
rubrics_metrics.description: First Aid Rule 1.--Aid breathing: loosen collar, waist bands, and unhook corset; Rule 2.--Protect from injury: gently restrain from falling or rolling against furniture; lay flat on bed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 3.--Protect tongue from being bitten: open jaws and put between teeth a rubber eraser tied to stout string, or rubber stopper tied to stout string. Rule 4.--Crush pearl of amyl nitrite in handkerchief and hold close to patient's nose and mouth till face is red and patient relaxes. Rule 5.--Let patient sleep after fit without rousing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution about dangerous measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Footnote cautions: Certain measures are dangerous and should be used only on physician's order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text flags dangerous interventions (e.g., chemical agents, potent drugs) and indicates they require physician authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isolation of febrile children with eruptive contagious fevers
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep any child with a fever isolated, even if the trouble seems to be due to a 'cold' or digestive disturbance, to avoid possible communication of the disorder to other children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Isolation means the sick child stays in a room by himself, doors kept closed, no children enter, and no objects in the room are removed to other parts of the house after beginning of patient's occupancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek physician and report contagious diseases
rubrics_metrics.description: The services of a physician are particularly desirable in all eruptive contagious diseases to make an early diagnosis and to protect family, neighbors, and community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to secure medical aid for children is regarded by the law as criminal neglect; boards of health require reporting of contagious diseases as soon as their presence is known; failure to comply may render offender liable to fine or imprisonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scarlet fever — incubation and contagious period guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Period of Development: after exposure usually from two to five days. Duration of Contagion: commonly considered contagious only so long as peeling of the skin lasts, but catarrhal secretions may be infectious for many days after other evidences are past.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scarlet fever patients should always be isolated for as long a period as six weeks—and better eight weeks—without regard to any shorter duration of peeling, and if peeling continues longer, isolation should continue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scarlet fever — monitoring for complications
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequent complications include enlarged glands under jaw/neck, joint pain and swelling, inflammation of kidneys (noted toward end of second week), middle ear inflammation with abscess and possible deafness, inflammation of eyelids, heart damage (valvular trouble), blindess and nervous disorders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examination of the urine by the attending physician at frequent intervals is essential; watch for puffiness of eyelids/face, reduced urine output, dark smoky urine as signs of kidney involvement. Spray the nose and throat frequently and use ear protection (nightcap with earlaps) if room is not warm to help prevent ear complications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scarlet fever — home treatment when physician unobtainable
rubrics_metrics.description: Put patient to bed in the most airy, sunshiny room heated to 70°F with flannel nightgown and light bed clothing. Use cold sponging to overcome fever and diminish nervous symptoms; body sponged part at a time with water about 70°F, place a wet ice cap over forehead; dry thoroughly after sponging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeat sponging when temperature is over 103°F. If chill after sponging, place a hot-water bag at the feet. Keep a rubber bag of ice or cold cloth on the head continually. Throat: spray hourly with hydrogen peroxide full strength; nose with peroxide diluted 1:1 three times daily. Surround outside of throat with ice bag or cold cloth covered with oil silk and flannel. Diet: milk, broths, thin gruels, plenty of water. Rub sweet oil or carbolized vaseline over whole body night and morning during illness and convalescence. Keep bowels regular (injections or mild cathartics). Nurse and mother should wear a gown and cap over outside clothes and remove them in hall when leaving sick room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measles — environment and isolation
rubrics_metrics.description: Put patient to bed in a darkened, well-ventilated room at temperature of 68–70°F. Adopt all possible precautions; keep other children from school and away from companions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Isolation may often fail to prevent spread in the house because measles can be infectious before rash appears, but it is still recommended to limit spread outside the home.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measles — fever management and sponging
rubrics_metrics.description: If fever is over 103°F and accompanied by distress and restlessness, children may be sponged with tepid water; adults with water at 80°F, every two hours or so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the directions given under scarlet fever for sponging and drying; use ice/cold cloth on head if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measles — hot pack (mustard blanket) for cough or poor rash development
rubrics_metrics.description: When cough is incessant or the rash does not come out well, use the hot pack: strip patient and wrap from feet to neck in a blanket wrung out of hot water containing two teaspoonfuls of mustard stirred into a gallon of water; cover with two dry blankets and allow patient to remain two or three hours, may be repeated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep a cold cloth on the head during the process. This is recommended as beneficial when cough is severe or rash is sluggish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measles — cough and hoarseness remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Cough mixture: syrup of ipecac 20 drops and paregoric one teaspoonful for an adult (one-third dose for a six-year-old), given in one-quarter glass of water and may be repeated every two hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If hoarseness, rub neck with mixture of sweet oil (two parts) and oil of turpentine (one part) and cover with flannel bandage. Cough mixture will tend to relieve condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measles — eye care and diarrhea treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Eye care: a solution of boric acid (10 grains to the ounce of water) is to be dropped in both eyes every two hours. Severe diarrhea: use bismuth subnitrate one-quarter teaspoonful every three hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eye symptoms may be severe and require special treatment to prevent impaired vision; treat diarrhea promptly to avoid dehydration and complications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measles — diet and convalescence duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Diet: milk, broths, gruels, raw eggs; for infants dilute usual milk mixtures one-half with barley water. Nourishment every two hours except during sleep. Patient should be ten days in bed and should remain three days in his room after getting up (or three weeks in all, if there are others who may contract measles in the house), and after leaving his room should stay in the house a week longer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principal danger after measles is lung trouble (pneumonia or tuberculosis); avoid exposure to wet or cold drafts during recovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: German measles — diagnostic differentials and identifying features
rubrics_metrics.description: German measles is distinct from measles and scarlet fever. It often has no catarrhal symptoms; rash may be the first sign and usually appears first on face then chest, covering whole body in hours. Glands at back of neck are characteristic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Period of development usually about two weeks (may vary 5–18 days). Fever is often mild (~100°F) or absent. Diagnosis aided by mild preliminary symptoms, absence of prolonged cough, and presence of posterior cervical gland enlargement.
